stages.name: Frame
stages.line: Turn a research question into a data hypothesis, and plan for your wellbeing.

stages.name: Find
stages.line: Search deliberately, so you can defend what you found and what you didn't.

stages.name: Preserve
stages.line: Archive and log sources before they disappear.

stages.name: Verify
stages.line: Test the connection between a piece of content and the claim made about it.

stages.name: Analyze
stages.line: Make sense of large collections of documents, images, video, audio and networks.

stages.name: Protect
stages.line: Reduce exposure to distressing material and keep sensitive files off third-party servers.

worksheets.title: Psycho-Social Threat Modeling
worksheets.summary: Identify risks to your wellbeing and your teammates', and plan how to reduce them before, during and after an investigation.

worksheets.title: From Research Question to Data
worksheets.summary: Break a research question into its parts, find proxies that offer indirect evidence, and form a data hypothesis.

worksheets.title: Digital Landscape Assessment
worksheets.summary: Work with your team to map the platforms, languages, producers and formats where your data is likely to be.

worksheets.title: Searching for Data: a Data Discovery Framework
worksheets.summary: Think about data relationally: where it is produced, how it is shaped, and where it is likely to live.

worksheets.title: Advanced Search Operators Quick Reference
worksheets.summary: A one-page reference for exact phrases, exclusions, site and file-type searches, date ranges and more.

worksheets.title: Creating a Programmable Search Engine
worksheets.summary: Build a Google search engine over sources you choose, trading completeness for precision and less personalization.

worksheets.title: Doing a Systematic Sweep Search
worksheets.summary: Slice a long, noisy search into time windows so you can make defensible claims about completeness, and even absence.

worksheets.title: Archiving Basics
worksheets.summary: From a better browser history to the Internet Archive and scripted archiving: keep a research trail you can trace back.

worksheets.title: Installing the Save to Sheets Extension
worksheets.summary: Set up the Save to Sheets extension so your team can collect URLs and their metadata in one shared spreadsheet.

worksheets.title: Digital Verification
worksheets.summary: The verification workflow through technical, content and source analysis, and how to archive and report the results.

tools.name: Sidekick
tools.summary: A browser sidebar that does what the Claude for Chrome extension does, using a local model in LM Studio, so nothing you read or ask about leaves your machine.
tools.needs: Needs Chrome on a laptop or desktop.

tools.name: QueryForge
tools.summary: A GDELT query builder with a bundled directory of news outlets by country, for monitoring coverage of an event.

tools.name: Deep Research Agent
tools.summary: Local agentic research in the browser over a Google Programmable Search Engine, so you control the sources the model reads.
tools.needs: Downloads a language model of a gigabyte or more the first time, and works best on a laptop or desktop with a recent browser.

tools.name: Canary
tools.summary: Collects GDELT, Google News, Media Cloud, X, Bluesky and Telegram results in the background into an inbox you triage, tag and export.
tools.needs: Needs Chrome on a laptop or desktop.

tools.name: HRC Archiver
tools.summary: Bellingcat's Auto Archiver with a graphical interface and without the Google integrations, for archiving links to video, images and social media posts.

tools.name: Save to Sheets
tools.summary: Capture web pages, search results and posts to a shared Google Sheet with one click.
tools.needs: Needs Chrome on a laptop or desktop.

tools.name: Geolocator
tools.summary: 2D and 3D maps, satellite imagery, line-of-sight, sun elevation and shadow analysis in one place.
tools.needs: Best on a laptop or desktop.

tools.name: Kiln
tools.summary: Search Sentinel-2 imagery by visual similarity, detect land-cover change, or teach it a concept from a few painted examples.
tools.needs: Best on a laptop or desktop.

tools.name: EmbedScape
tools.summary: Explore text, images or video by meaning: see semantic clusters and search within the collection.
tools.needs: Downloads an image model the first time you open it.

tools.name: Jepa! Jepa!
tools.summary: Cluster images and video by visual similarity and run reverse image search over your own collection.
tools.needs: Downloads about 600 MB of image models the first time you open it.

tools.name: Videologue
tools.summary: Build a catalogue of the faces, people, vehicles and buildings that appear across hours of video.
tools.needs: Best on a laptop or desktop.

tools.name: B-RAG
tools.summary: Build a database from your documents and ask questions of it with a local model.

tools.name: HRC Transcribe
tools.summary: Extract the audio from video and transcribe it with Whisper, entirely in the browser.
tools.needs: Downloads a large speech model the first time, and is much faster on a computer with a recent graphics card.

tools.name: HRC Translate
tools.summary: Translation in the browser with Meta's NLLB-200, covering more than 200 languages including many minority languages.
tools.needs: Downloads a translation model of several hundred MB the first time you open it.

tools.name: Schuim Surfer
tools.summary: Network analysis of social media data collected with Zeeschuimer, with signals of coordinated inauthentic behavior.
tools.needs: Best on a laptop or desktop.

tools.name: Event Data Explorer
tools.summary: Map and filter event data, or start from a sample dataset.

tools.name: Censorama
tools.summary: Blurs human shapes in video so you can look for contextual clues with less exposure to distressing content.

tools.name: HRC Share
tools.summary: Peer-to-peer file transfer between devices, with no server in the middle.
